items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Scandal Escalates: Federal Prosecutors Launch Criminal Probe into Clippers' Salary Cap Circumvention
items.summary: The LA Clippers are now facing a federal criminal investigation into allegations of salary cap circumvention involving Kawhi Leonard. This comes after the NBA levied historic penalties against the team, including forfeiting five first-round picks, a $30 million fine, and suspensions for owner Steve Ballmer and team executives. Leonard himself was fined $700,000, and his uncle, Dennis Robertson, received a five-year NBA ban for his involvement.

items.headline: Clippers Eye Darius Garland Trade to Recoup Draft Capital Amid Penalties
items.summary: Following the severe NBA sanctions and a new federal probe, the Clippers are reportedly considering trading guard Darius Garland to recover some of the five first-round draft picks they forfeited. Garland is seen as one of the team's most valuable assets, with Kawhi Leonard also expected to be traded to the Toronto Raptors.

items.headline: Pelicans Finalize Bennedict Mathurin Contract After Cap-Clearing Trade
items.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans have finalized a two-year, $16 million contract with Bennedict Mathurin. To create the necessary salary-cap room, the Pelicans traded Jordan Hawkins and Micah Peavy to the Memphis Grizzlies in exchange for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson.

items.headline: Mavericks Focused on Cooper Flagg's Development, Kyrie Irving in Trade Talks
items.summary: Despite insisting Kyrie Irving is part of their 2026-27 plans, the Dallas Mavericks are reportedly building their roster around 2026 Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, leading to trade speculation around Irving, who is recovering from a torn ACL.

items.headline: Lakers Continue Pursuit of Wing/Forward Help, Eyeing Dalton Knecht, Jarred Vanderbilt Trades
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers are still actively looking to upgrade their wing and forward positions and are reportedly exploring trades involving young role players Dalton Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt.

items.headline: Six-Team Blockbuster Sends D'Angelo Russell to Memphis, Khris Middleton to Washington
items.summary: A significant six-team trade has been completed, with veteran guard D'Angelo Russell heading to the Memphis Grizzlies and Khris Middleton joining the Washington Wizards via a sign-and-trade deal. This complex transaction reshapes multiple rosters across the league.

items.headline: Jalen Duren Considers Qualifying Offer Amid Stalled Contract Negotiations with Pistons
items.summary: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren, an All-NBA player last season, is reportedly leaning towards playing on his $9.6 million qualifying offer in the upcoming season if a long-term deal isn't reached by the end of September. Duren seeks a five-year, $200 million contract, while the Pistons are offering closer to $175 million over five years.

items.headline: Lonnie Walker IV Inks Non-Guaranteed Training Camp Deal with Nuggets
items.summary: Veteran shooting guard Lonnie Walker IV has officially signed a non-guaranteed training camp deal with the Denver Nuggets. Walker joins other new additions to the Nuggets roster, including Alpha Diallo, Marvin Bagley III, and DeMar DeRozan.

items.headline: Ben Simmons Signs One-Year, Non-Guaranteed Deal with Kings
items.summary: Ben Simmons has signed a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the Sacramento Kings. The deal offers the former All-Star an opportunity to make the roster ahead of the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Several Teams Announce New Head Coaches for 2026-27 Season
items.summary: The NBA offseason has seen a flurry of coaching changes. Dusty May has taken the helm for the Dallas Mavericks, Tiago Splitter is now the head coach of the Chicago Bulls, and Mike Brown has been hired by the New York Knicks. Other notable hires include Taylor Jenkins for the Milwaukee Bucks, Jamahl Mosley for the New Orleans Pelicans, Sean Sweeney for the Orlando Magic, and Micah Nori for the Portland Trail Blazers.

items.headline: 2026-27 NBA Season Key Dates Announced
items.summary: The 2026-27 NBA regular season is scheduled to commence on October 20, 2026, and conclude on April 11, 2027. Training camps for some teams, including the Rockets and Mavericks, are set to open on September 22.

items.headline: Russell Westbrook and Kyle Lowry Announce Retirements
items.summary: Two prominent veterans, Russell Westbrook and Kyle Lowry, announced their retirements from professional basketball earlier in the offseason. Westbrook concluded an 18-season career in August, while Lowry retired in July after 20 seasons, including an NBA championship with the Raptors.
